html:
The Great Depression was the worst economic collapse of the industrial age, lasting from 1929 through most of the 1930s. It began in the United States and spread to almost every country through trade and money.

The Wall Street crash of October 1929 opened it. Thousands of American banks failed, and by 1933 about a quarter of American workers had no job. Countries raised tariffs to protect themselves, and world trade shrank by more than half. Nations tied to the gold standard were squeezed hardest; those that left it, as Britain did in 1931, tended to recover sooner.

Its effects reached far:

  • Food and raw material exporters such as Australia, Argentina and Canada saw prices collapse. Newfoundland went broke and gave up self-rule in 1934.
  • In Siam, budget cuts helped bring on the revolution of 1932.
  • In Germany mass unemployment helped Hitler into power in 1933.
  • In the United States Franklin D. Roosevelt's New Deal put people to work on public projects, while the Dust Bowl drove farm families west.
  • New Zealand's Social Security Act of 1938 was one of many welfare laws the crisis inspired.

The economist John Maynard Keynes argued that governments should spend to fight slumps. Rearmament and World War II finally ended the depression. Its memory shaped how governments handled the 2008 financial crisis.
sum: The Great Depression was the worst economic collapse of the industrial age, lasting from 1929 through most of the 1930s. It began in the United States and spread to almost every country through trade and money.
